narratives: Statement from groundskeeper William: "I heard the revolver go off at some point after I started my shift. Some point later, at least an hour, Col. Mustard left arrived at the house and greeted me. Nice man, complimented the flowers."
Evidence report: "A fiber was found on the candlestick. We have identified this to be some kind of sheeps wool. All suspect, apart from Col. Mustard, were wearing some kind of garment made of wool."

We interviewed the house clearner, Ms. Baker. She stated she looked at the watch on her left hand an it read 4PM when Ms. Scarlet entered the house. She further said she looked at the watch on her right hand and it read 1PM  when she first witnessed the rope.  We concluded one of these watches is broken but Ms. Baker could not attest to which watch she wore on which hand.

Witness statement from the maid; "I was in charge of serving tea to all the guests. I don't remember what time I served each guest. Oh, but I do remember Prof. Plum requested ice tea. I had to  start his quickly after Miss White, as the tea needed to be chiilled for at least an hour."

We questioned Prof. Plum and Ms. Scarlet under polygraph. Prof. Plum stated he had no contact with the candlestick. Ms. Scarlet stated she was not there at 1PM. The polygraphs showed only one of these to be a lie, however our intern  didn't write down which was which. He had since been let go.

narratives: Statement from groundskeeper William: "I heard the revolver go off at some point after I started my shift. Some point later, at least an hour, Col. Mustard left arrived at the house and greeted me. Nice man, complimented the flowers."
Evidence report: "A fiber was found on the candlestick. We have identified this to be some kind of sheeps wool. All suspect, apart from Col. Mustard, were wearing some kind of garment made of wool."

We interviewed the house clearner, Ms. Baker. She stated she looked at the watch on her left hand an it read 4PM when Ms. Scarlet entered the house. She further said she looked at the watch on her right hand and it read 1PM  when she first witnessed the rope.  We concluded one of these watches is broken but Ms. Baker could not attest to which watch she wore on which hand.

Witness statement from the maid; "I was in charge of serving tea to all the guests. I don't remember what time I served each guest. Oh, but I do remember Prof. Plum requested ice tea. I had to  start his quickly after Miss White, as the tea needed to be chiilled for at least an hour."

We questioned Prof. Plum and Ms. Scarlet under polygraph. Prof. Plum stated he had no contact with the candlestick. Ms. Scarlet stated she was not there at 1PM. The polygraphs showed only one of these to be a lie, however our intern  didn't write down which was which. He had since been let go.
